clinical_observations.content: Sabrina participated in an in-clinic evaluation with her mother present. She presented with a cheerful and cooperative affect initially, though her attention span fluctuated significantly, requiring frequent redirection. Muscle tone was noted to be within normal limits, and joint range of motion was adequate for her age. Sabrina demonstrated a tendency toward distractibility, especially in less structured tasks, necessitating maximal verbal and visual cues to sustain task involvement. Engagement patterns varied, as Sabrina showed more consistent task participation in self-directed activities. Fine motor coordination and visual-motor skills were assessed to be developing, with specific tasks requiring hand-over-hand assistance to achieve completion. These observations, particularly the need for frequent assistance and cues, impacted the validity of standardized testing outcomes and necessitated modifications for a more accurate assessment of abilities.
